entries.title: Wood and anger
entries.content: In traditional East Asian medicine, Wood is linked with the liver and with anger, frustration and resentment. Its healthy side is drive and growth.
entries.source: 5 Elements (Wu Xing): The Five Elements Theory in Chinese Medicine
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Fire and over-excitement
entries.content: Fire is linked with the heart and with 'joy' in the sense of agitation or over-excitement. Its healthy side is warmth and connection.
entries.source: 5 Elements (Wu Xing): The Five Elements Theory in Chinese Medicine
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Earth and worry
entries.content: Earth is linked with digestion and with overthinking and worry. Its healthy side is steadiness and care for others.
entries.source: 5 Elements (Wu Xing): The Five Elements Theory in Chinese Medicine
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Metal and grief
entries.content: Metal is linked with the lungs and breathing and with sadness and grief. Its healthy side is clarity and letting go.
entries.source: 5 Elements (Wu Xing): The Five Elements Theory in Chinese Medicine
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: Water and fear
entries.content: Water is linked with the kidneys and with fear and dread. Its healthy side is courage and willpower.
entries.source: 5 Elements (Wu Xing): The Five Elements Theory in Chinese Medicine
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: The balancing cycle
entries.content: The tradition says elements restrain each other: grief (Metal) cools anger (Wood), and fear (Water) calms too much joy (Fire). Some Chinese hospitals use this idea in 'five-element' talk therapy.
entries.source: Application of Psychotherapy Based on Five-Element Theory in TCM - PMC
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection

entries.title: How Giun uses this
entries.content: Talk it through pairs the feeling linked to today's element with a real psychology tool, like a cool-down break for anger or checking the evidence for worry. The tradition gives the lens; the tool is from research.
entries.label: Tradition - for reflection
